record.title: The additive-complexity regularity conjecture for automatic sequences
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and let $\mathbf{w}=w_0w_1w_2\cdots$ be a $k$-automatic sequence, meaning that its $k$-kernel

$$
\{(w_{k^e n+c})_{n\geq 0}\mid e\geq 0,\ 0\leq c<k^e\}
$$

is finite. For each $n\geq 1$, let $\rho^+_{\mathbf{w}}(n)$ denote the number of distinct digit sums of the length-$n$ factors occurring in $\mathbf{w}$. A sequence is **$k$-regular** if the $\mathbb{Z}$-module generated by its $k$-kernel is finitely generated.

**Additive-complexity regularity conjecture.** The sequence $(\rho^+_{\mathbf{w}}(n))_{n\geq 1}$ is $k$-regular.

The conjecture proposes that additive complexity preserves the regularity structure associated with automatic sequences. The paper establishes this property for the specific Thue–Morse-like sequence generated by $0\mapsto01$, $1\mapsto12$, and $2\mapsto20$, but no resolution of the general assertion is provided in the source.
record.source_name: Jin Chen, Zhixiong Wen and Wen Wu, “On the additive complexity of a Thue-Morse like sequence”, arXiv:1802.03610 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03610

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

record.title: Marušič–Scapellato–Zagaglia Salvi compatibility conjecture
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph. Its canonical double cover has adjacency matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&A\\A&0\end{pmatrix}$ when $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $\Gamma$. The matrix $A$ is **compatible** if there is a nonidentity permutation matrix $P$ of the same size such that $AP$ is the adjacency matrix of some graph. A graph is **vertex-determining** when distinct vertices have distinct neighborhoods. **Marušič–Scapellato–Zagaglia Salvi's compatibility conjecture.** A connected non-bipartite vertex-determining graph is unstable if and only if it has a compatible adjacency matrix. The source notes that every nontrivially unstable graph has a compatible adjacency matrix, while the conjecture asserts the converse for connected non-bipartite vertex-determining graphs. The paper's preceding theorem establishes that no arc-transitive nontrivially unstable circulant exists, but does not state a resolution of this broader conjecture.
record.source_name: Yan-Li Qin, Binzhou Xia and Sanming Zhou, “Stability of circulant graphs”, arXiv:1802.04921 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04921

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

record.title: Fuller–Gould conjecture on dense $K_4^-$-saturated graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_4^-$ be the graph obtained from the complete graph $K_4$ by deleting one edge. A graph is **$K_4^-$-saturated** if it contains no copy of $K_4^-$, but adding any missing edge creates at least one copy of $K_4^-$. Write $[a,b]=\{a,a+1,\ldots,b\}$.

**Fuller–Gould conjecture.** The $K_4^-$-saturated graphs with sizes in the interval

$$
\left[\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-n+7,\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil\right]
$$

are of two types: complete bipartite graphs with partite sets of nearly equal size, and 3-partite graphs with two partite sets of nearly equal size and one partite set of order one.

This conjecture describes the structure of $K_4^-$-saturated graphs whose numbers of edges are close to the extremal value $\left\lfloor n/2\right\rfloor\left\lceil n/2\right\rceil$. The cited work establishes the preceding range of edge sizes up to one below the interval's lower endpoint, while the proposed structural classification for this dense range is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Jun Gao, Xinmin Hou and Yue Ma, “The edge spectrum of K_4^--saturated graphs”, arXiv:1804.10359 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.10359

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: The partition-weight conjecture in dimensions divisible by four
record.statement:
Let $d\geq4$ with $d\equiv0\pmod4$, and let $\pi=\{\pi_{i_1\ldots i_{d-1}}\}_{i_1,\ldots,i_{d-1}\geq1}$ be a $(d-1)$-partition. Let $\mathsf{w}_\pi$ be the signed fixed-point weight determined by the unique orientation from the orientation uniqueness conjecture, and let $L_\pi$ denote the corresponding line-bundle factor. **Partition-weight conjecture.** After specializing $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_{d-1}=\lambda_d=0$,

$$
L_\pi(0,0,\ldots,-\ell)\,\mathsf{w}_\pi=(-1)^{|\pi|}\omega_\pi\prod_{m=1}^{\pi_{1\cdots1}}(\ell-(m-1)),
$$

for some $\omega_\pi\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, and this positive rational coefficient equals the combinatorial weight $\omega^c_\pi$ defined by decompositions of $\pi$ into binary representations of nonempty $(d-2)$-partitions. The conjecture gives a combinatorial interpretation of the fixed-point contributions and is supported by the calculations described in the paper.
record.source_name: Yalong Cao and Martijn Kool, “Counting zero-dimensional subschemes in higher dimensions”, arXiv:1805.04746 (2018).

record.title: C$_2$MS model-checking algorithm for graphs of bounded rank-width
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\phi(\mathcal{X})$ be a C$_2$MS formula, and let $\alpha$ be an assignment to its free variables. Write $\operatorname{qr}(\phi)$ for the quantifier rank of $\phi$ and $\operatorname{rwd}(G)$ for the rank-width of $G$. Then there is a computable function $f$ such that the following holds. **C$_2$MS rank-width conjecture.** There exists an algorithm which decides whether

$$
G\models\phi(\alpha(\mathcal{X}))
$$

and whose running time is

$$
\mathcal{O}\bigl(f(\operatorname{qr}(\phi),\operatorname{rwd}(G))\cdot |G|^3\bigr).
$$

This would extend the known fixed-parameter model-checking bounds for monadic second-order logic on graphs of bounded clique-width to the counting extension C$_2$MS and rank-width. The conjecture is presented as an expected algorithmic extension, and its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Extension of the mixed double-dimer construction to all self-intersecting contours
record.statement:
Let

$$
\{z_{i,j,k}^{(4)}: \left(-k < i,j, i+j < k-1 \mathrm{~for~} k > 0\right) \mathrm{~~and~~} \left( k-1 < i,j, i+j < -k \mathrm{~for~} k \leq 0 \right) \}
$$

be the three-dimensional space of toric cluster variables described in the source. For self-intersecting contours, consider subgraphs with vertices of multiplicity one and two, using mixed configurations in which vertices have multiplicity $1$ except for a simply-connected interior region of vertices of multiplicity $2$. **Extension conjecture.** The construction rule inspired by the family $\varphi\left(A(0,0,n+2)\right)=z_{0,0,n+1}^{(4)}$ extends to all other self-intersecting contours, with an analogue of the taut condition for crossing the inner double-dimer region, and degenerates to the usual dimer-only rule when the self-intersection disappears, namely when $i$, $j$ or $i+j$ falls outside of $[-k,k-1]$ or $[k-1,k]$. The source gives no evidence of resolution.

record.title: Ding–Li conjecture on 2-designs from ternary linear codes
record.statement:
Let $m\ge 3$ be an odd integer, let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of $\operatorname{GF}(3^m)$, and let $\mathcal C_1$ and $\mathcal C_2$ be the ternary linear codes defined by

$$
\mathcal{C}_1=\left\\{ \left( \operatorname{Tr}_{3^m/3}\left( a \alpha^{4i}+b \alpha^{2i} \right) \right)_{i=0}^{\frac{3^m-1}{2}-1}:a,b\in \operatorname{GF}(3^m)\right\\},
$$

and

$$
\mathcal{C}_2=\left\\{ \left( \operatorname{Tr}_{3^m/3}\left( a \alpha^{\left(3^{\frac{m-3}{2}}+1\right)i}+b \alpha^{\left(3^{\frac{m-1}{2}}+1\right)i} \right) \right)_{i=0}^{\frac{3^m-1}{2}-1}:a,b\in \operatorname{GF}(3^m)\right\\},
$$

where $\operatorname{Tr}_{3^m/3}$ is the trace from $\operatorname{GF}(3^m)$ to $\operatorname{GF}(3)$. For $i\in\\{1,2\\}$, write $A_k(\mathcal C_i)$ for the number of codewords of weight $k$, and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i)$ and $\mathcal B_k(\mathcal C_i)$ denote the point set and the supports of the weight-$k$ codewords, respectively. **Ding–Li's 2-design conjecture.** If $k$ is an integer satisfying $A_k(\mathcal C_i)>1$, then

$$
(\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i),\mathcal B_k(\mathcal C_i))
$$

is a $2$-design. This is one of the conjectured infinite families of $2$-designs arising from linear projective ternary codes; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Chunming Tang, Cunsheng Ding and Maosheng Xiong, “Steiner systems S(2, 4, 3^m-12) and 2-designs from ternary linear codes of length 3^m-12”, arXiv:1901.09228 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09228

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Ding–Li conjecture on 2-designs from dual ternary codes
record.statement:
Let $m\ge 3$ be an odd integer, let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of $\operatorname{GF}(3^m)$, and let $\mathcal C_1$ and $\mathcal C_2$ be the ternary linear codes defined above. For $i\in\\{1,2\\}$, let $\mathcal C_i^{\perp}$ be the dual code, write $A_k(\mathcal C_i^{\perp})$ for the number of its codewords of weight $k$, and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i^{\perp})$ and $\mathcal B_k(\mathcal C_i^{\perp})$ denote its point set and the supports of its weight-$k$ codewords. **Ding–Li's dual 2-design conjecture.** If $k$ is an integer satisfying $A_k(\mathcal C_i^{\perp})>1$, then

$$
(\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i^{\perp}),\mathcal B_k(\mathcal C_i^{\perp}))
$$

is a $2$-design. This extends the proposed design property to every nontrivial weight class of the dual codes; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Chunming Tang, Cunsheng Ding and Maosheng Xiong, “Steiner systems S(2, 4, 3^m-12) and 2-designs from ternary linear codes of length 3^m-12”, arXiv:1901.09228 (2019).

record.title: The mod-9 q-series conjectures
record.statement:
For $q$ a formal variable and $(a_1,\ldots,a_r;q^9)_\infty=\prod_{m\geq0}\prod_{j=1}^r(1-a_jq^{9m})$, the five partition conjectures are equivalently expressed by the following $q$-series identities. **Mod-9 q-series conjectures.**

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q,q^3,q^6,q^9;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+n_1+3n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q^2,q^3,q^6,q^7;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+2n_1+3n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q^3,q^4,q^5,q^6;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+n_1+2n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}=\frac{1}{(q^2,q^3,q^5,q^8;q^9)_\infty},
$$

$$
\sum_{\substack{n_1\geq0\
_2\geq1}}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+n_1+4n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}+\sum_{\substack{n_1\geq0\
_2\geq1}}\frac{q^{n_1^2+3n_1n_2+3n_2^2+2n_1+4n_2+1}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}+\sum_{n_1\geq0}\frac{q^{n_1^2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}}=\frac{1}{(q^1,q^4,q^6,q^7;q^9)_\infty}.
$$

These identities remain unproved, although analytic sum-sides for the partition families have been found.

record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.05199

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

record.title: The ternary tenth-power block-size conjecture
record.statement:
Let $m\geq 3$ be odd, and define $k_m$ recursively by

$$
k_m=\frac{3^m+1}{2}+3^{m-1}-3k_{m-2},\qquad k_1=2.
$$
 For $b,c\in {\mathrm{GF}}(3^m)$, let $B_{(x^{10},b,c)}$ denote the corresponding block, and let ${\mathcal{B}}_{(x^{10},k)}$ be the collection of distinct blocks of size $k$. **The ternary tenth-power block-size conjecture.** The block sizes and multiplicities are

$$
|B_{(x^{10},b,c)}|=\begin{cases}\frac{3^m+1}{2}&\text{for }3^m\text{ choices of }(b,c),\\k_m&\text{for }(3^m-1)3^m\text{ choices of }(b,c),\end{cases}
$$

and

$$
|{\mathcal{B}}_{(x^{10},(3^m+1)/2)}|=3^m,\qquad |{\mathcal{B}}_{(x^{10},k_m)}|=\frac{3^m(3^m-1)}{2}.
$$
 Further, the first incidence structure is a symmetric $2$-$(3^m,(3^m+1)/2,(3^m+1)/4)$ design arising from the squares in ${\mathrm{GF}}(3^m)$, and the second is a $2$-$(3^m,k_m,k_m(k_m-1)/2)$ design. This is described as a fundamental open problem concerning designs supported by monomials over odd-characteristic finite fields.
record.source_name: Cunsheng Ding and Chunming Tang, “Combinatorial t-designs from special polynomials”, arXiv:1903.07375 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07375

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2019). “The following is a fundamental open problem.”

record.title: The extended designs from Payne, Cherowitzo and Subiaco o-polynomials
record.statement:
Let $m\geq 5$ be odd, set $q=2^m$, and let $\hat{\mathbb{D}}(f,k)=({\mathrm{GF}}(q),\hat{\mathcal{B}}_k)$ be the extended construction, with $k=q/2$. Define the listed o-polynomials by

$$
\operatorname{Payne}(x)=x^{5/6}+x^{3/6}+x^{1/6},
$$

$$
\operatorname{Cherowitzo}(x)=x^{2^e}+x^{2^e+2}+x^{3\cdot 2^e+4},\qquad e=(m+1)/2,
$$

with its reciprocal variant

$$
\overline{\operatorname{Cherowitzo}}(x)=x^{q-2^e}+x^{q-2^e-2}+x^{q-3\cdot 2^e-4},
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{Subiaco}_1(x)=(x+x^2+x^3+x^4)(x^4+x^2+1)^{q-2}+x^{2^{m-1}}.
$$
 **The extended special-o-polynomial design conjecture.** For any of these four choices of $f$, $\hat{\mathbb{D}}(f,q/2)$ is a $3$-$(q,q/2,(q-4)(q-1)q/8)$ design. The claim gives explicit further examples of $3$-designs from the extended construction beyond the already covered o-monomial cases. It is stated without a supplied resolution status, so it remains open in this record.
record.source_name: Cunsheng Ding and Chunming Tang, “Combinatorial t-designs from special polynomials”, arXiv:1903.07375 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07375

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2019). “The following is a fundamental open problem.”

record.title: Hazrat–Roozbeh's graph-algebra classification conjecture
record.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be finite graphs, let $k$ be a field, let $C^*(E)$ and $C^*(F)$ denote their graph $C^*$-algebras, let $L_k(E)$ and $L_k(F)$ denote their Leavitt path algebras, and let $\H_0^{\operatorname{gr}}(\mathcal{G}_E)$ and $H_0^{\operatorname{gr}}(\mathcal{G}_F)$ be the zeroth graded homology groups of the associated étale graph groupoids. **Hazrat–Roozbeh's conjecture.** The following are equivalent: (1) there is a gauge-preserving isomorphism $C^*(E)\to C^*(F)$; (2) there is a graded ring isomorphism $L_k(E)\to L_k(F)$; and (3) there is an order-preserving $\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]$-module isomorphism

$$
H_0^{\operatorname{gr}}(\mathcal{G}_E)\longrightarrow H_0^{\operatorname{gr}}(\mathcal{G}_F)
$$

that preserves the order unit, sending $[1_{\mathcal{G}_E^{(0)}}]$ to $[1_{\mathcal{G}_F^{(0)}}]$. This conjecture proposes a common classification invariant for finite graph $C^*$-algebras and Leavitt path algebras; its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Pere Ara, Roozbeh Hazrat and Huanhuan Li, “Graded K-Theory, Filtered K-theory and the classification of graph algebras”, arXiv:1904.06468 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06468

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Conjecture on cocyclic Hadamard matrices of order 4p
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $W,X,Y,Z$ be circulant blocks defining cocyclic Hadamard matrices of order $4p$. Write $\tau$ for the relevant nontrivial action and $\iota$ for the inversion action. **The cocyclic Hadamard matrix conjecture.** There are no cocyclic Hadamard matrices of the forms

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc} W & -X & -Y & -Z\\ X & -W & -Z & -Y\\ Y & -Z & -W & -X\\ Z & -Y & -X & -W \end{array}\right]
$$

and

$$
\left[\begin{array}{llll} W & -X & -Y & -Z\\ X & -W & -Z & -Y\\ Y^{\mathsf T} & -Z^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} & -X^{\mathsf T}\\ Z^{\mathsf T} & -Y^{\mathsf T} & -X^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} \end{array}\right].
$$

For $p\equiv 1\pmod 4$, there exist cocyclic Hadamard matrices of the form

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc} W & X & Y & Z\\ X^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} & Z^{\mathsf T} & -Y^{\mathsf T}\\ Y^{\mathsf T} & Z^{\mathsf T} & -W^{\mathsf T} & -X^{\mathsf T}\\ Z & -Y & -X & W \end{array}\right],
$$

with circulant blocks $W,X,Y,Z$, and these matrices are not equivalent to a Williamson-type matrix or a (transposed) Goethals–Seidel matrix, yielding a new family of cocyclic Hadamard matrices. The first nonexistence assertions correspond respectively to the actions $(\tau,\tau)$ and $(\tau,\iota)$, while the existence assertion corresponds to $(\iota,\iota)$ in the $L_{1,1,0}$ construction.
record.source_name: Santiago Barrera Acevedo, Heiko Dietrich and Padraig O Cathain, “Constructing cocyclic Hadamard matrices of order 4p”, arXiv:1904.11460 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.11460

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Frankl's conjecture of order $k|\ell$
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{A}_{k|\ell}$ be the class of union-closed families used in the paper, and let $\mathfrak{c}_{k|\ell}$ denote the corresponding supremal proportion of members meeting a $k$-element subset in at least $\ell$ elements. **Frankl's conjecture of order $k|\ell$.** If $\mathcal{A}\in\mathfrak{A}_{k|\ell}$, then there exists $S\subseteq\bigcup\mathcal{A}$ with $|S|=k$ such that at least

$$
2^{-k}\sum_{i=\ell}^k\binom{k}{i}
$$

of the members $A\in\mathcal{A}$ satisfy $|A\cap S|\geq\ell$; equivalently,

$$
\mathfrak{c}_{k|\ell}=2^{-k}\sum_{i=\ell}^k\binom{k}{i}.
$$

In particular, $\mathfrak{c}_{k|1}=2^{-k}(2^k-1)$, $\mathfrak{c}_{k|k}=2^{-k}$, and $\mathfrak{c}_{2k+1|k+1}=2^{-1}$. These variants refine the original Frankl conjecture by prescribing the size and intersection threshold of the witnessing subset; their general validity is open.
record.source_name: Maysam Maysami Sadr, “A Note on the Frankl Conjecture”, arXiv:1907.09976 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09976

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Kogan's five-type classification conjecture for triples of triangles
record.statement:
A **linking of triangles** is a set of pairwise disjoint, non-degenerate triangles in 3-space; triangles are understood as their outlines, with unnumbered vertices and no orientation. Two linkings are **combinatorially isotopic** if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of elementary moves, where an elementary move replaces one triangle $ABC$ by $ABC'$ while the swept triangular regions remain disjoint from every other triangle.

**Kogan's classification conjecture.** Any linking of three non-ordered triangles is combinatorially isotopic to one of the following five types: three triangles whose convex hulls are pairwise disjoint; the Borromean or Valknut linking; a Hopf linking of two triangles together with a third triangle whose convex hull is disjoint from the first two; a triangle together with two triangles whose convex hulls are disjoint and both intersect the first triangle at exactly one point; or the specified linking formed by an equilateral triangle and two successive rotations by $\pi/3$ and translations by $\vec h$, where $3\vec h$ is the altitude of the preceding triangle. Linkings from different types should not be combinatorially isotopic.

This conjecture proposes a complete classification of three-triangle linkings under combinatorial isotopy. The paper proves that the standard triple and the Borromean triple are not combinatorially isotopic, but the proposed completeness of the five-type list remains open.
record.source_name: E. Kogan, “Linking of three triangles in 3-space”, arXiv:1908.03865 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03865

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

record.title: The inertia–bicoloring conjecture for full-rank typical graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a full-rank typical graph. A **$G$-partial matrix** is a partial symmetric matrix whose specified off-diagonal entries correspond to the edges of $G$; it is **minimally completable to full rank** if it has a completion of full rank but no proper submatrix obtained by deleting a specified entry has this property. Write $G^c$ for the complement of $G$, and let $\operatorname{In}(M)=(m,n,0)$ denote the common inertia of all completions of $M$, with $m$ positive and $n$ negative eigenvalues. A **proper bicoloring** of $G^c$ assigns red or blue to every vertex so that adjacent vertices have different colors. **Inertia–bicoloring conjecture.** There exists a $G$-partial matrix $M$, minimally completable to full rank, with $\operatorname{In}(M)=(m,n,0)$ if and only if $G^c$ has a proper bicoloring with $m$ red vertices and $n$ blue vertices. The conjecture characterizes the possible inertias of minimally full-rank-completable partial matrices in terms of proper two-colorings of the complement. The stated evidence is that the authors found no full-rank typical graph and corresponding partial matrix whose inertia failed to arise from such a coloring; the general characterization remains open.
record.source_name: Daniel Irving Bernstein, Grigoriy Blekherman and Kisun Lee, “Typical ranks in symmetric matrix completion”, arXiv:1909.06593 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.06593

record.title: Interval decomposition conjecture for the nesting-poset zigzag module
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset, and let $\field P$ denote its incidence algebra. For the critical and regular levels $a_0,t_1,a_1,t_2,\dots,t_n,a_n$ associated with the Morse function $f$, let $\field N_{a_i}$ and $\field N_{t_i}$ be the corresponding incidence algebras of nesting posets. **Interval decomposition conjecture.** There is a zigzag module of $\field$-algebras

$$
\field N_{a_0}\leftrightarrow\field N_{t_1}\leftrightarrow\field N_{a_1}\leftrightarrow\field N_{t_2}\leftrightarrow\cdots\leftrightarrow\field N_{t_n}\leftrightarrow\field N_{a_n},
$$

with arrow direction given by Corollary 1, that decomposes into a sum of interval indecomposables of the form

$$
\field_I(t)=\begin{cases}\field\{*\}&\text{if }t\in I\\0&\text{if }t\notin I.\end{cases}
$$

Furthermore, this collection of interval indecomposables determines $f$ up to poset equivalence. This is presented as a structural persistence claim for the nesting posets; the supplied text gives no evidence of resolution, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Michael J. Catanzaro, Justin Curry, Brittany Terese Fasy, Jānis Lazovskis, Greg Malen, Hans Riess, Bei Wang and Matthew Zabka, “Moduli Spaces of Morse Functions for Persistence”, arXiv:1909.10623 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.10623

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

record.title: q-gamma positivity conjecture for alternating Eulerian polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $\operatorname{altdes}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{altmaj}(\pi)$ denote the alternating descent number and alternating major index of $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$. Define the bivariate alternating Eulerian polynomial by 
$$
\widehat{A}_n(t,q)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n}t^{\operatorname{altdes}(\pi)}q^{\operatorname{altmaj}(\pi)}.
$$
 **q-gamma positivity conjecture.** The polynomial $\widehat{A}_n(t,q)$ has the expansion 
$$
\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n}t^{\operatorname{altdes}(\pi)}q^{\operatorname{altmaj}(\pi)}=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}\widehat{\gamma}_{n,k}(q)q^{\binom{k+1}{2}}(-t)^k\prod_{i=k+1}^{n-1-k}(1+tq^i),
$$
 where $\widehat{\gamma}_{n,k}(q)\in\mathbb{N}[q]$ and $(1+q)^k$ divides $\widehat{\gamma}_{n,k}(q)$. This is presented as an alternating analogue of the known $q$-$\gamma$-positivity expansion for Eulerian--Mahonian polynomials; the claimed coefficient positivity and divisibility are not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Zhicong Lin, Shi-Mei Ma, David G. L. Wang and Liuquan Wang, “Positivity and divisibility of alternating descent polynomials”, arXiv:2011.02685 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: Coefficientwise total-positivity conjecture for the four-parameter recurrence triangle
record.statement:
Let $a,c,d,e$ be algebraic indeterminates, and define $T(n,k)$ by

$$
T(n,k)=[a(n-k)+c]T(n-1,k-1)+(dk+e)T(n-1,k)
$$

for $n\geq 1$, with $T(0,k)=\delta_{k0}$. Thus $\bm{T}=(T(n,k))_{n,k\geq 0}$ is a lower-triangular matrix over $\mathbb{Z}[a,c,d,e]$. A polynomial is nonnegative in the coefficientwise order when all its coefficients are nonnegative, and a polynomial matrix is **coefficientwise totally positive** when all its minors have nonnegative coefficients. **Four-parameter coefficientwise total-positivity conjecture.** The lower-triangular matrix $\bm{T}$ defined by the recurrence above is coefficientwise totally positive in the indeterminates $a,c,d,e$. This conjecture would imply the clean Eulerian and reversed Stirling conjectures under the specializations $(a,c,d,e)=(1,1,1,1)$ and $(1,0,0,1)$, respectively; the source gives no proof of the general assertion.
record.source_name: Xi Chen, Bishal Deb, Alexander Dyachenko, Tomack Gilmore and Alan D. Sokal, “Coefficientwise total positivity of some matrices defined by linear recurrences”, arXiv:2012.03629 (2020).

record.title: Infinitesimal rigidity of hinged spanning cycles on the hypercube
record.statement: Let the $n$-Roberts graph encode the facet adjacencies of the $n$-cube, and let a **hinged spanning cycle** be a spanning cycle of this graph whose corresponding $2n$ facet adjacencies are retained as hinges while all other ridges are removed. **Infinitesimal rigidity conjecture.** All spanning cycles of the $n$-Roberts graph, corresponding to hinged spanning cycles of facets on the $n$-cube, produce an infinitesimally rigid structure: there is no non-trivial first-order deformation that restricts to an infinitesimal congruence on each facet. This conjecture concerns the rigidity of prefabricated hypercube structures formed by hinging facets along the edges of a spanning cycle; establishing it would explain why such structures can be transported in a folded state before unfolding after an additional cut.
record.source_name: Kristin DeSplinter, Satyan L. Devadoss, Jordan Readyhough and Bryce Wimberly, “Unfolding cubes: nets, packings, partitions, chords”, arXiv:2007.13266 (2020).
